result.title: Screening for nonrigidity in structure from motion using projected reprojection residuals
result.comment: 34 pages including 19 pages of supplementary material. 5 main figures and 5 supplementary figures
result.summary: Sparse structure from motion (SfM) assumes a static scene, yet deformation may still yield plausible reconstructions. Reprojection-error summaries discard how errors are arranged across points and views. We propose a diagnostic that first removes residual components explainable by small point and camera adjustments and simple spatial trends that change over time. It then measures alignment with fixed spatial and temporal patterns. The diagnostic uses one estimated SfM reconstruction and provides screening evidence rather than a physical deformation estimate. Across four synthetic tubular families, the diagnostic detected all eight acquisitions with prescribed motion, compared with five or six for summaries of reprojection-error magnitude. Each family's cutoff was the highest static score among the other three families, so the static acquisition with the highest score also screened positive. With the same cutoffs, the diagnostic retained positive detections in 19 of 20 reconstruction variants spanning changes in appearance and reconstruction pipeline, with one numerical abstention. These findings show that the arrangement of reprojection errors across points and views can reveal inconsistencies that their magnitudes alone miss. The four families were known during development, and the transfer variants reused two of them. Within this setting, the diagnostic offers a practical way to flag a plausible reconstruction for closer inspection using only its estimated cameras, 3D points and image observations.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一种 SfM 非刚性形变筛查诊断：先剔除可由小幅点/相机调整与简单时空趋势解释的残差成分，再测量剩余残差与固定时空模式的对齐程度，仅用一次重建给出筛查证据而非形变估计。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 VLM 推理无直接关系，但其「剥离可解释 nuisance 成分后再看残差排列」并可主动弃权的思路，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据可信度筛选与停止/复核判定提供可核查的诊断模板。
